blocks.content: Under Article 3 of the Indian Constitution, Parliament has the exclusive power to alter the boundaries or change the name of any State by passing a law by simple majority.

rows: Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands (Alteration of Name) Act, 1973

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 3 of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to alter the names, boundaries, or areas of existing states.
United Provinces was renamed Uttar Pradesh in 1950, becoming the first state in independent India to undergo a name change.
Madras State was renamed Tamil Nadu in 1969 through the Madras State (Alteration of Name) Act, 1968.
Mysore State was renamed Karnataka and Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands were renamed Lakshadweep in 1973.
Uttaranchal was renamed Uttarakhand in 2006, Pondicherry was renamed Puducherry in 2006, and Orissa was renamed Odisha in 2011.
A bill for renaming a state can be introduced in Parliament only with the prior recommendation of the President of India.
The President refers the bill to the concerned state legislature for its views within a specified period, but Parliament is NOT bound by the state legislature's opinion.
Renaming a state under Article 3 requires a Simple Majority in Parliament and is NOT considered an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.
